what: The Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya's medicine — the eight branches, the three doṣas with five subtypes each, the seven constituents and three wastes, the six tastes and potencies, daily and seasonal regimen, rejuvenation and virility — which reappears, with Buddhist causation and other additions, in the Four Tantras.
era: 8th–12th c. (translations; compilation of the Four Tantras)

evidence.detail: Tibetan translations of Indian medical works in the Tengyur's medical section: Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya (D4310) with commentaries (D4311, D4312), Yogaśataka (D4306), Jīvasūtra (D4307)
Same eight branches (with women's diseases for śālākya), same doṣa and dhātu scheme, five subtypes of each doṣa with corresponding functions, element-pairs of the tastes (bitter differs)
The Four Tantras is the Medicine Buddha's word translated from an Indian original by Vairocana (the tradition does not describe it as a borrowing)
The Four Tantras was compiled in the 12th c. with the Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya as a principal source, together with Chinese (notably pulse) and Greco-Arabic elements (labelled scholarly metadata)

what: The Kālacakra tantra and Vimalaprabhā, the six-branch vajra-yoga, the empty forms and unchanging bliss, and the 'emptiness endowed with all supreme aspects', which Dolpopa identifies with the other-empty ultimate; also the Kālacakra's account of the ages.

evidence.detail: Dolpopa's Mountain Doctrine and Fourth Council cite the Kālacakra and Vimalaprabhā throughout
Lineage from Somanātha through Yumo Mikyö Dorje; Künpang Thukje Tsöndrü's seventeen lineages

what: The view of the Perfection of Wisdom — emptiness of all phenomena, the teaching on māras — applied as the practice of cutting self-clinging.

evidence.detail: Chöd root texts are titled instructions (man ngag) of the Perfection of Wisdom (catalogue P000053, P000138)
Machig's realization while reciting the Perfection of Wisdom

what: Padampa Sangye's instructions, counted as the 'father lineage' of Chöd.

evidence.detail: Machig received instruction from Padampa Sangye

what: The other-emptiness view, presented by Kongtrul as the Great Madhyamaka, and the Jonang Kālacakra six-branch yoga and hundred instructions, preserved in the Treasury of Instructions.

evidence.detail: Kongtrul's tenet presentation and Uttaratantra commentary
The Kālacakra six-branch yoga counted among the eight chariots

what: The siddha instructions Padampa Sangye is said to have received from many Indian masters.

evidence.detail: Padampa's biographies list many Indian teachers
